AbortReason.description:
The network error an aborted request reports to its page, under
Playwright's names.

Acted.description:
What a locator action answers once its input landed on its target:
nothing, since no operation returns a handle on an element (ADR 0085).

Actor.description: Who an entry's event was done by.

oneOf.description: A person, by the name their account or OS user goes by.
A named token (area 12), by its name.
A Client, by the surface its `hello` named.

AllowanceSource.description: What set the Memory allowance: the tightest of them (ADR 0040).

oneOf.description: The process's own cgroup's memory limit, v1 or v2.
The Windows Job object the process runs in.
Half of physical memory, when nothing tighter applies.

AppliedLimit.description:
A Limit that applies to a Run (ADRs 0041 and 0101): its scope's kind and
ID, what it caps, its period, what it allows, what is left of it and who
set it.

amount.description: What it allows per period: a count, or millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

left.description: What is left of it in the current period.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

resets_at.description: When its period starts again; none for a Limit without one.

scope.description: What it is on; a scope kind this reader does not know is kept.

name.description:
Its name as published: a package or crate name, a file name, or an
OCI reference without its tag.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of what `url` serves.

ArtifactId.description: Which Pinned artifact: its kind, its name and its build.

ArtifactKind.description:
What a Pinned artifact is (ADR 0098: the clean-up's rule covers every
kind). An entry of a kind the engine does not know is one it cannot read,
and keeps.

oneOf.description: A browser build, such as Chrome for Testing's.
The versioned copy of an executable a Daemon runs from (ADR 0024).
The engine executable a Product's Rust crate downloads (ADR 0051).

Asked.description: The format, with its default options.

AttemptError.description: The error an attempt failed with.

details.description:
The error's own details, as its Error code defines them, such as the
time a site's `Retry-After` asked for and a `fix`; left out when it
has none.

Attestation.description:
A Sigstore attestation bundle, checked offline with `gh attestation
verify --bundle` (ADR 0066).

sha256.description: The SHA-256 digest of the bundle.

url.description: Where the bundle is downloaded from.

AuditEntry.description: One entry of the Audit log, as its hash covers it.

details.description:
What its kind records, such as a Secret reference and the domain it
was sent to, never a secret's value.

kind.description: Its kind, a value of the shared type `audit_kind`.

layer.description:
The settings layer its event came from, such as an Operator policy
that switched a control off; none where no layer applies.

run_id.description: The Run it happened in; none outside a Run.

sequence.description: Its place in the chain, from 1.

surface.description:
The surface the actor acted through, such as `console` for a person
in the Console; none for the engine's own events.

entries.description: How many entries the log holds.

first_broken.description:
The first sequence that does not verify: an entry edited, missing
or out of its place, or, past the last entry, a tail the head file
says was there; none when intact.

intact.description:
Whether every entry chains to the one before it and the head file
agrees with the last one.

AxisReason.description: One reason a Run is not `verified` or not `complete` (ADR 0029).

call_id.description:
The AI task it is about, by its `callId`, when it is about one (ADR
0100).

code.description:
What it is, such as `stopped` or `failed`; a reason this reader does
not know is kept as it is.

BlockCause.description: Why a site refused a page (ADR 0035), on the wire as written.

oneOf.description: A page that checks the browser before it lets it through.
A page that asks a person to prove they are human.
The site refused because too many requests came too fast.
The site refused the address the request came from.

A trap page a person would never reach, such as a labyrinth of
hidden links; only Foxhound's Frontier produces it (ADR 0095).
The site asked to be paid for the page (ADR 0045).
A wall that asks for consent before it shows the page (ADR 0048).

BodyHandle.description: A page body as a handle: its ID, the file that holds it and its size.

body.description: Its ID, the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its bytes.

path.description: The file that holds it, which a Client on the same machine reads.

run_id.description: The Run whose folder holds it.

BrowserCacheEntry.description:
One Pinned artifact's entry in the Browser cache, `entry.json` beside its
files: what it is, the digest its files have, and when it was installed
and last used, which the clean-up reads (ADR 0098).

digest.description: The digest of its files, `sha256:<hex>`, which every launch checks.

format_version.description: The version of this format the entry was written in.

installed_at.description: When it was installed, in RFC 3339.

used_at.description: When it was last launched or installed, in RFC 3339.

BrowserName.description: A browser family, as ADR 0056 names them.

deleted.description: What it deleted, or would delete under `--dry-run`.

dry_run.description: Whether it only listed what it would delete.

not_cleaned.description: Why it cleaned nothing, when it did not run.

artifacts.description:
Each Pinned artifact of the Product version, and what installing it
did.

CancelParams.description: What `$/cancel` names: the call to stop.

mode.description:
The mode it ran in, such as `attached` or `daemon`, when the case
runs in several.

capability.description: The capability the case belongs to.

case.description: The case's ID in the declared case list.

evidence.description: What it saw: the oracle's answers, the scripted messages.

mode.description:
The mode it ran in, such as `attached` or `daemon`, when the case
runs in several.

runtime.description: The runtime it ran on, such as `node-24` or `cpython-3.14`.

oneOf.description: Every entry has checks and every check held.
A check failed, or an entry holds no check.
The case log holds no entry for it.

CaseResult.description: One case of a capability, with its derived outcome.

entries.description:
One entry per time the case ran, such as once per mode; none when it
was not reached.

id.description: The case's ID in its suite.

CertificatePin.description:
One pin of the known-certificates store, as `certs.list` answers it and
as the store's rows hold it: a host whose certificate was accepted on
first use, and the key it must keep presenting.

changed_spki_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the key the host presented instead, which stopped it
with `certificate_changed`, as `sha256/` and its standard base64: the
key `certs.accept` pins in its place. None while no change waits.

host.description: The host, as the URL parser leaves it.

pinned_at.description: When it was pinned; none when the row cannot be read.

run_id.description:
The Run whose connection pinned it; none outside a Run or when the
row cannot be read.

spki_sha256.description:
The SHA-256 of the pinned certificate's `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`, as
`sha256/` and its standard base64; none when the row cannot be read,
which stops the host as a changed key.

CertsAcceptParams.description:
What `certs.accept` takes: the host, and the changed key the person
accepts, as `certs.list` shows it.

host.description: The pinned host, as the URL parser leaves it.

spki_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the changed key, as `sha256/` and its standard base64.

host.description: The pinned host, as the URL parser leaves it.

forgotten.description: Whether the caller had a pin for it, now removed.

Check.description: One check of a Journey's outcome.

surfaces.description:
The surfaces of the variants the check belongs to, when it belongs
to some only, such as an SDK package's install checks; every variant
when empty. A `foxhound-cli` variant takes the `cli` variant's.

task.description: A Proving ground task the oracle must answer `verified` for.

oneOf.description: An earlier failure stopped the variant before it.

task.description: The task whose oracle answer the check reads, when it names one.

text.description: The check's text in the Journey.

Checkpoint.description:
A Checkpoint as the engine reports it (ADRs 0002, 0102 and 0116): a
consistent, self-contained copy of a Run's state, complete at its
location before it is reported, from which the Run resumes on this
machine or another one.

digest.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, in lowercase hexadecimal.

journal_position.description:
The position of the run's journal it holds: how many commits of the
run file it contains. A resume from it redoes the work after.

location.description: Where it is: the file's path on the engine's machine.

run_epoch.description:
The run epoch of the writer that took it (ADR 0003), which a
destination compares and sets: one older than it holds is refused.

Chunk.description: What `$/chunk` carries: the next bytes of the body a call reads.

data.description: Its bytes, in Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding).

offset.description: Where its bytes start in the body.

ClickParams.description: What `locator.click` takes: the locator whose element it clicks.

ClientPackages.description: The Collie client packages, one per language (ADR 0095).

CommandError.description:
A failed command's error: what a Client's error object holds, with the
operation the command called.

code.description: The Error code, or the name of the protocol failure.

group.description: The group of the Error code, named for its remedy (ADR 0079).

message.description: What went wrong, for people; never matched on.

operation.description:
The operation the command called, by its canonical name, such as
`run.finish`; absent when the command failed before it could call
one, as `npx @goodfetch/collie` does when it finds no executable.

retryable.description: Whether the same call may succeed when made again.

CommandFailed.description: What a command prints under `--json` when it fails.

Completeness.description:
Whether a Run's results cover everything in its scope (ADRs 0005 and
0029).

oneOf.description: It finished, but the engine cannot vouch that nothing was missed.

keys.description:
The keys to explain, each a key or a prefix of keys, such as
`timeout`; every key when empty.

origin.description:
Where those run values come from: a scope's `settings` option by
default, or the CLI's flags when the CLI asks a Daemon.

project.description: The project configuration to explain with.

settings.description:
Run-layer values to explain with, as a Run's `settings` would give
them.

ConformanceDocument.description:
A `conformance` document: each declared capability's outcome, derived
from its cases.

online.description:
Whether the Proving ground was the online copy, whose results report
and never block a release.

proving_ground.description: The Proving ground the cases ran against.

runtime.description:
The runtime the cases ran on, such as `rust`, `node-24` or
`cpython-3.14`.

ConsoleFailure.description:
Why a Daemon's Console did not start: an Error code, its message and
what to do instead.

signed_out.description: How many sign-ins it ended: every one.

ConsoleLocation.description:
Where a console message was written: its script's URL and position, as
the browser counts them from 0.

url.description: The script's URL; empty for a script the page evaluated.

ConsoleMessage.description: What `page.console` reports: a message the page wrote to its console.

text.description:
Its text: each argument, a primitive as its value and any other as
the browser describes it, joined by spaces.

type.description:
Its type as Playwright names it, such as `log`, `warning` or
`error`.

ConsoleOpened.description:
What `console --json` prints (ADR 0069): the Console's sign-in link,
whose fragment carries the token the page swaps once for its cookie
(ADR 0024), the URL the command opened the browser on, or would have.

ConsoleState.description:
Where a Daemon's Console is, as its runtime file and `daemon status`
report it.

oneOf.description: The Console is served at this URL, such as `http://127.0.0.1:7801/`.
The Console did not start; the Daemon still serves its Clients.
The engine carries no Console, as an SDK crate's linked engine.

CountOf.description: How many requests ended for one reason, code or cause.

CpuReading.description: The engine's CPU and Tokio workers, as the governor read them.

busy.description:
The engine's CPU time since the last sample, in percent of its
allowance.

parallelism.description:
How many threads the engine may run at once, its CPU allowance
(`available_parallelism`, which honours a cgroup's quota).

tokio_busy.description: The Tokio workers' busy time since the last sample, in percent.

CrawlRequest.description: One work item of a crawl as its handler receives it (ADR 0093).

body.description: The body it is sent with, if any.

method.description: The method it is sent with.

CrawlRequestEnqueueParams.description:
What `crawl_request.enqueue` takes: one request to add, from one attempt
of a crawl request.

body.description: The body it is sent with, if any.

crawl_request_id.description: The ID of the crawl request whose attempt enqueues.

document.description:
The document the handler read, whose base URL a relative `url`
resolves against; absent, the crawl request's own URL is the base.

forefront.description:
Whether it goes ahead of every request its domain holds pending,
whatever their priority, as Crawlee's `forefront` (ADR 0005): of two
such requests, the later goes first. A priority or `forefront` never
orders requests of different domains (ADR 0004); `false` by default.

key.description:
Its identity in the Frontier, declared by the program in place of
its method, its URL's key and its body's hash: a canonicalization
of the program's own, which always wins (ADR 0005).

lease_epoch.description: The attempt's lease epoch, as `crawl_request.handle` gave it.

method.description: The method it is sent with: `GET` by default.

payload.description: The data the program attaches for its handler.

priority.description:
Its priority among the requests of its domain: higher goes first; 0
by default.

url.description: The URL to add, absolute or relative to the document's base URL.

CrawlRequestHandleParams.description:
What `crawl_request.handle` gives the handler: one attempt of one work
item, under its lease.

lease_epoch.description: The lease's epoch, which only goes up (ADR 0003).

session.description: The Session of the crawl's Session pool that serves the attempt.

CrawlRequestHandled.description:
What a handler answers once its attempt returned: the outputs it staged,
which commit once, under the attempt's lease (ADR 0003), or its skip.

records.description: The Records it pushed, in order.

skipped.description:
Its handler's skip: the request ends `skipped` with the reason
`handler`, and the attempt's Records are discarded.

CrawlRequestOutcome.description:
How one crawl request ended (ADRs 0079 and 0102). A request that
`run.retry_failed` re-admits ends again, and its later outcome
supersedes this one: a reader keys outcomes by `request.id`.

oneOf.description: Its handler returned, and what it staged was committed.

nothing_committed.description: Why it committed no Record, when it committed none.

records.description:
Per Dataset its handler pushed into, the Records committed,
dropped and rejected.

oneOf.description: Its last attempt failed, and no retry is left.

message.description: The handler's or the Hook's own text.

attempts.description: How many attempts it took: retries are a count, not an outcome.

errors.description: The error of each failed attempt, in order.

position.description:
Its place in the Run's commit order, from 1, which `run.outcomes`'s
`after` takes.

ended.description:
Whether the sequence is over: the Run has ended, or has no live
writer, and nothing committed after `next` matches.

next.description: The position the next page starts after.

outcomes.description: The outcomes that match, in commit order.

CrawlRunReport.description:
A crawl's Run report (ADR 0102): what a crawl adds to every Run's
report, a part no area supplied being absent. On the wire, a crawl's
parts sit beside every Run's, which a reader of [`RunReport`] keeps among
its `kind_parts`.

checkpoint.description: The last Checkpoint written of it in this engine, when one was.

completeness.description: Whether its results cover its scope.

completeness_reasons.description: Why it is not `complete`, when it is not.

console_url.description:
Its page in the Console, where its Run trace replays, when the
engine knows a Console address (ADR 0031).

error.description:
The error the call that ends it raises: the one that failed a
`failed` Run, or a write at its end that failed, such as its Plan
file's (ADR 0116).

nothing_done.description: Why the call that answered it did nothing, when it did nothing.

plan.description: What it did with its Plan file (ADR 0091).

policy_version.description:
The version of the Operator policy it ran under, when one applied
(ADR 0031).

recording.description: What it did with the Response recording its start named (ADR 0105).

settings.description:
Each effective value it ran with, the layer that set it and the one
that locked it, as `config.explain` gives them (ADR 0028).

sinks.description: Each Sink that applies to it (ADRs 0026 and 0103).

sitemaps.description: Its sitemaps, as its progress gives them.

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped, when it did.

uncertain_effects.description:
Each Effect it left uncertain, until a person reconciles it (ADR
0106).

usage.description:
What it used, as the Usage ledger charged it, with the Limits that
apply to it (ADR 0101).

verdict.description: Whether its own checks prove what it committed.

verdict_reasons.description: Why it is not `verified`, when it is not.

warnings.description: What the areas warn of, each with a code and a message.

weakened.description: Every setting that weakened a safeguard for it (ADR 0028).

project.description: The project configuration the Client found, layer 3 (ADR 0083).

run_id.description: The Run's ID, as `run.start` takes it.

seeds.description: The requests the crawl starts from.

settings.description: The Run's settings, nested by key: the run layer (ADR 0083).

CreditParams.description:
What `$/credit` grants: more events, or chunks, for a streaming call;
sent by the engine, more seeds a `run.add_seeds` call takes.

credits.description:
How many more events, or chunks, the Client takes; sent by the
engine, how many more seeds the call takes.

DaemonEndpoint.description:
Where a Daemon or an Attached engine's private endpoint listens (ADR
0024): a `0600` Unix socket on macOS and Linux, loopback TCP on
Windows.

DaemonHealth.description:
What `daemon.health` answers: what the ops listener's `/livez` and
`/readyz` check (ADR 0050). In a Daemon group, readiness ignores the
Lead Daemon's reachability.

live.description:
Whether it is live: its runtime and its Runs' registry, which writes
their run state, respond.

ready.description: Whether it is ready: live, and able to take a new Run.

unready.description: Why it is not ready, when it is not; empty when it is.

daemon.description:
What the Daemon answered, or `None` when no Daemon of the major
answered.

healthy.description: Its answer, which its exit code repeats: 0 when `true`.

stopped.description:
What the Daemon running before answered when it was stopped so the
service could take its place, or `None` when none ran.

What the Daemon running with the old token answered when it was
stopped, or `None` when none ran.

token_file.description: The file that holds the new persistent token, mode `0600`.

started.description: Whether this command started it, rather than finding it running.

clients.description: How many Clients are connected, the caller and Consoles included.

console.description: Where its Console is served, or why it is not.

kept_alive.description:
Whether it never stops idle: `--keep-alive`, a held Schedule or an
installed service.

live_runs.description: How many of its Runs are live.

product.description: The Product the Daemon runs as.

daemon.description: The running Daemon, or `None` when none runs.

runtime_file.description: The runtime file of the executable's major.

service.description:
The per-user service `daemon install` registered for the major, or
`None` when none is installed.

stopped.description: What the stopped Daemon answered, or `None` when none ran.

DaemonStopping.description: What `daemon.stop` answers, before the Daemon stops.

live_runs.description: How many live Runs it stops, each resumable from its own state.

removed.description: The service it removed, or `None` when none was installed.

DatasetRecords.description:
What a succeeded request's commit did with its Records in one Dataset
(ADR 0103).

rejected.description: How many the Dataset's schema rejected.

total_bytes.description: The bytes the answer announced, when it did.

EndingError.description: An Error code a Run's ending raises, with its message and details.

product.description: The Product the engine runs as.

product_major.description: The major of its Product version, which names its per-major state.

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

EngineInstance.description: One engine process, new each time an engine starts: the positions of its events count within it. A Client compares it for equality only.

EnqueueDocument.description: The document a handler read, against which its relative URLs resolve.

base_href.description: The `href` of its first `<base>` element, as written.

url.description: The URL the document was reached at, after every redirect.

Enqueued.description:
The Frontier's answer to a seed or an enqueue (ADRs 0079 and 0093): a
value, never an error, since a request is one among many.

oneOf.description: The Frontier admitted it as a crawl request.

id.description: The crawl request's ID within the Run.

url.description:
Its URL as the WHATWG URL Standard parsed it, resolved against
its base: the URL its handler receives.

oneOf.description: The Frontier did not admit it.

url.description: Its URL as it was given.

EnqueuedBatch.description:
What `$/enqueued` carries: the answer of each seed of one `$/seeds`
batch, in the batch's order.

ErrorData.description:
What a failure's `data` holds: its Error code, whether the same call may
succeed when made again, and the code's own details.

code.description: The Error code, or the name of the protocol failure.

retryable.description: Whether the same call may succeed when made again.

ErrorGroup.description: The seven groups of Error codes, named for their remedy (ADR 0079).

oneOf.description: A policy, a Limit, a lock or a person refused.
The page or site never reached the state the call needed.
The Model provider's answer was unusable.
Something Goodfetch depends on is unreachable or gone.

code.description:
One of JSON-RPC's predefined codes for a protocol failure; otherwise
the numeric class of the Error code's group, from −32000 to −32099.

data.description: The Error code and its details.

message.description: What went wrong, for people; never matched on.

ErrorResponse.description: The reply to a call that failed.

id.description: The call's id, or `null` when the engine could not read one.

EventBatch.description:
What `$/events` carries: a batch of one subscription's events, in the
order of their positions.

id.description: The id of the subscription's `events.subscribe` call.

data.description: Its payload, of the type the catalog gives the event.

dropped.description:
For a telemetry event, how many of the same kind and scope it
replaced unsent.

event.description: The catalog's name of the event.

after.description:
The last event the Client read, `{engine_instance, position}`: the
subscription resumes after it, or starts with `events.resync` when
the engine no longer holds it or another engine instance gave it, as
after a Daemon restart. Absent, it starts with the next event.

system_info.description:
Whether it also takes `engine.system_info`, the Resource governor's
periodic readings; false by default, so a subscription that reads
only what changes sees no periodic event.

Evidence.description: What a test saw, beside its checks.

messages.description:
The scripted messages exchanged, for a Client conformance case (ADR
0069).

observations.description:
What the Proving ground observed on the server side, as it reported
it.

Executable.description:
The executable a Journey variant drove: its Product and the Product
version it reports (ADRs 0084 and 0090).

oneOf.description: A Product's executable, which can run its major's Daemon.

A program that links the engine through a Product's Rust crate: its
builds are kept, but it never runs the Daemon.

ExplainedSetting.description: One setting as `config explain` shows it.

applied.description:
Whether this engine applies it: `false` for a key only the other
Product honours, which a shared file may hold (ADR 0087).

cap.description: An Operator policy's cap on it, if any.

locked_by.description:
The layer that locked it, if any: an Operator policy's lock, a
Recipe that declares it without exposing it, or the default for an
honesty guarantee.

origin.description: For the run layer, where the value came from.

products.description: The Products that honour it, from its Product mark (ADR 0095).

value.description:
The effective value, or for a key this engine does not apply, the
value its highest layer wrote.

weakens.description:
Whether its value weakens a guarantee class or switches off a costly
control, which the results it touches are marked with (ADR 0028).

requests.description: The latest outcome of each such request, in commit order.

FeatureId.description: A Feature's ID, `<kind>:<id>`, such as `row:CO-18` or `story:3-18`.

FillParams.description:
What `locator.fill` takes: the locator whose field it fills, and the
text.

value.description: The text the field holds afterwards; an empty text clears it.

Form.description:
The form a Client's user writes names in (ADR 0099), which the engine
renders the names and targets of its messages in.

oneOf.description: The TypeScript SDK, and Code mode.
The MCP server and the Framework adapters.

The catalog's own names: the Console, Integrations and the HTTP
listener.

FormatsParams.description: What `page.formats` takes: the page, and the formats it asks for.

FormatsRequest.description:
The formats a `page.formats` call asks for, each `true` or its options:
one value, which a Record can carry and a Dataset's schema can be
generated from (ADR 0103). A format left out is left out of the result.

markdown.description: The page's content as Markdown, with GFM's tables.

GotoParams.description:
What `page.goto` takes: the page, the URL it goes to, and when it
answers.

wait_until.description: When the navigation answers; `load` when absent.

GovernorLevel.description: How loaded the engine is, as its governor judges it.

oneOf.description: Every reading has headroom: concurrency may rise.
Memory passed `governor.critical`, or the host's is critical.

HandlerSkip.description: A handler's skip of its request: `ctx.skip(message)` (ADR 0093).

HealthProbe.description: Which of the ops listener's probes `daemon health` answers.

oneOf.description: `/readyz`'s: whether it is ready to take a new Run.

form.description:
The form its user writes names in (ADR 0099); none until each
surface names its own.

log_level.description:
The level of the engine's log events the Client receives as `$/log`
notifications, until `connection.set_log_level` changes it; none,
as `off`, receives none (ADR 0078).

needs.description:
The Product the Client needs, which every surface but a Browser
host's must name (ADR 0095).

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the sender speaks.

token.description: The Daemon's token; an Attached engine needs none.

HelloResult.description: What an engine answers to a `hello` it accepts.

engine_instance.description:
The engine process, new each time an engine starts: the positions
of its events count within it, so a Client that meets a new one
resyncs (ADR 0031).

private_endpoint.description:
An Attached engine's private endpoint, reported to the Client of its
stdio alone: where that Client's `workers=N` handler processes, and a
Daemon forwarding a live action, connect (ADRs 0024 and 0031).

protocol_version.description: The protocol version the engine speaks.

HttpBody.description: The body a crawl request is sent with (ADR 0093): its bytes in Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding).

HttpMethod.description: The method a crawl request is sent with (ADR 0093): an RFC 9110 token, `GET` by default; `DELETE`, `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `POST` and `PUT` are uppercased as Fetch normalizes them, and `CONNECT`, `TRACE` and `TRACK` are refused.

HttpsUrl.description: An https:// URL with a host.

oneOf.description: It was downloaded and checked now.
It was already there, with its pinned digest.

InstalledArtifact.description: One artifact `browsers install` made sure of.

outcome.description: Whether it was downloaded now or already there.

InstalledExecutable.description: One executable that ran on this machine (ADR 0098).

copy.description:
Its versioned copy in the Browser cache, from which a Daemon runs
(ADR 0024), once one was made.

last_seen.description: When it last ran, in RFC 3339.

modified_at.description: When its file was last modified then, in RFC 3339.

path.description: Its absolute path when it last ran.

pins.description:
The browser builds and other cache downloads its version pins, its
versioned copy included once a Daemon runs from it.

product.description: The Product it is, or whose Rust crate it links.

size.description:
The size of its file in bytes then, which with `modified_at` tells
whether the file at `path` is still this executable.

InstalledExecutables.description:
The list of installed executables, `installed-executables.json` in
Goodfetch home (ADR 0098). Newer versions of the format only add, so an
engine keeps every entry and field it does not know when it rewrites the
list.

executables.description: One entry per executable, at one path and one Product version.

format_version.description: The version of this format the list was written in.

InstalledService.description:
The per-user service of one major that `daemon install` registered,
recorded in `daemon-service.json` in the major's per-major folder (ADRs
0024, 0031 and 0098): what starts the major's pick, from which versioned
copy, and the socket its service manager listens on for it.

executable.description:
The versioned copy in the Browser cache that the service starts,
which starts its major's pick.

files.description: The files that define it to the service manager.

manager.description: The service manager it is registered with.

name.description:
Its name there: a launch agent's label, a user unit's name without
its suffix, or a logon task's path.

socket.description:
The socket the service manager listens on and hands the Daemon it
starts at the first connection, or `None` where the OS has no socket
activation (Windows).

Journey.description:
One Journey: a goal a person reaches through its Product's public
surfaces, written as steps from a starting state to an outcome checked
from outside the engine (ADR 0063).

area.description: The number of the ADR 0037 area whose spec owns the Journey.

covers.description:
The Feature IDs the Journey exercises, each `<kind>:<id>`, such as
`row:CO-18` for a row of ADR 0037's matrix or `story:3-18` for a user
story.

goal.description:
What the person achieves and what MUST be true at the end, in RFC
2119 words, readable as a specification without the code. It never
changes under the Journey's ID.

id.description: `J-` and three to nine digits, equal to the file's name.

product.description:
The Product whose executable and SDK packages the Journey drives:
Collie when Collie carries every step, Foxhound otherwise (ADR 0094).

proving_ground.description:
The Proving ground data the Journey starts from; absent when its goal
touches no page.

reason.description: Why a retired Journey was retired.

replaced_by.description: The Journeys that hold a retired Journey's goal now, possibly none.

status.description: Whether the Journey is still run.

steps.description: The steps, in order, in declarative words.

surfaces.description:
Each surface the goal is reachable on, by its name in ADR 0063, with
the milestone by which that surface must prove it.

title.description: A short name in the glossary's terms.

next.description:
The next free Journey number: a new Journey takes it and increments
it in the same pull request, and every ID is below it.

JourneyDocument.description:
A `journey` document: one Journey variant's outcome, derived from its
steps, checks and oracle answers.

checks.description: Each check of the Journey's outcome, in its order.

proving_ground.description:
The Proving ground it started, for a Journey whose goal touches a
page.

steps.description: Each step of the Journey, in its order.

surface.description:
The variant's surface, by its name in ADR 0063, or `foxhound-cli`
for a Collie Journey's `cli` variant run on Foxhound's executable
(ADR 0094).

surface_package.description:
The surface's package, for a surface that has one (an SDK, the
Console's build, an adapter).

tasks.description:
Each Proving ground task the Journey names, in its order: once per
check naming it, each with the answer to that check's submission in
the checks' order, or once when no check names it.

test_errors.description:
Each error that failed the variant's test outside its steps, checks
and tasks, with its Error code: a page error or an accessibility
violation the test found once its body had ended (ADR 0068). A
variant with one is `failed`, whatever its steps and checks say.

JourneyId.description: A Journey's ID: `J-` and three to nine digits (ADR 0063).

JourneyOutcome.description:
A Journey variant's outcome. A declared variant with no document is
`unproved`, which the catalog report computes from the document's
absence (ADR 0063).

oneOf.description:
Every automated step and check passed, every named task is
`verified` and no error failed the test outside them.

KeyValueStoreDeleted.description: What `key_value_store.delete` answers once the key is gone.

KeyValueStoreKey.description: What `$/key` carries: the next key of the store a call lists.

KeyValueStoreKeyParams.description:
What `key_value_store.get` and `key_value_store.delete` take: the Run
and the key.

run_id.description: The Run whose store it is.

KeyValueStoreKeysEnded.description: What `key_value_store.keys` answers once it sent its last key.

KeyValueStoreKeysParams.description:
What `key_value_store.keys` takes: the Run, and the prefix every key it
sends starts with.

prefix.description: The prefix of the keys it sends; every key when left out.

run_id.description: The Run whose store it is.

KeyValueStoreSet.description: What `key_value_store.set` answers once the value is committed.

KeyValueStoreSetParams.description: What `key_value_store.set` takes: the Run, the key and its value.

run_id.description: The Run whose store it is.

value.description:
The value: any JSON but a top-level null, which `value_invalid`
refuses; a nested null is kept.

KeyValueStoreValue.description:
What `key_value_store.get` answers: the key's committed value, or null
when the key is absent.

value.description: The value, or null for an absent key.

target.description: How many the governor admits at once now.

KindUsage.description: What a Run used of one Usage kind.

amount.description: A count, or millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency, an ISO 4217 code; none for a count.

usage_kind.description: The Usage kind, a value of a type both Products share.

LastRead.description:
The last event a Client read: its position, and the engine instance
that gave it.

engine_instance.description: The engine instance, as its `hello` named it.

LearnedRule.description: A URL rule the Frontier learned (ADR 0005).

oneOf.description:
It ended early: by a Limit, an abort, its timeout, the loss of its
engine or exhausted resources.
An error in the engine or the program's code ended it.

Limit.description:
One Limit of the Usage ledger: a generic row, which a newer engine may
write with a scope kind, a Usage kind, a currency or a period this one
does not know (ADR 0041).

amount.description:
How much it allows per period: a count of the Usage kind, or
millionths of the currency.

currency.description:
The currency it caps the Usage kind's price in, an ISO 4217 code;
none for a Limit on the Usage itself.

must_understand.description:
Whether an engine that cannot evaluate it must refuse the runs it
cannot place outside it, with `limit_not_understood`.

period.description:
The period it counts over; none for a Limit that never starts again,
such as a Client connection's.

usage_kind.description: The Usage kind it caps, a value of a type both Products share.

LimitScope.description:
What a Limit is on: a scope kind, a value of a type both Products share
(`install`, `daemon`, `person`, `token`, `connection`, and Foxhound's
`partitioned_crawl`), and which one of its kind (ADR 0041). A kind this
reader does not know is kept as it is.

id.description:
Which one of its kind: the major's name for a Daemon, the person's
name, the token's name or the Client connection's ID; empty for the
install.

LimitSetter.description: Who set a Limit, which decides whether it allows paying (ADR 0045).

oneOf.description: A person, in the Console or an interactive CLI prompt.
A Client, which only adds a Limit of its own.

LimitStanding.description: What the engine that read a Limit makes of it.

oneOf.description: It holds its runs to it.

It is on a value only Foxhound carries, such as `paid_fetch`, which
a Collie engine keeps untouched (ADR 0098).
It cannot evaluate it: a newer engine wrote it.

LimitUsage.description: One Limit with the Usage counted against it in its current period.

charged.description:
The Usage charged in the current period: what ended runs used, and
what was reclaimed from dead engines' Slices.

held.description: The Usage live runs hold in Slices they have not returned yet.

left.description: What is left of the amount in the current period.

managed_major.description:
The major of the managed Operator policy whose row it is; none for
a row no managed policy wrote.

period_started_at.description: When the current period started; none for a Limit without one.

resets_at.description: When the next period starts; none for a Limit without one.

standing.description: What the engine that read it makes of it.

Locator.description:
A locator (ADR 0085): what an action looks for on a page, resolved
again at each use, never a handle on an element. This tracer's locators
are CSS selectors.

selector.description: A CSS selector, which also matches inside open shadow roots.

LogEvent.description: What `$/log` carries: one log event of the engine.

dropped.description:
How many log events the Connection was too slow to receive since the
one before: logs are telemetry, and never slow a Run.

target.description:
Where in the engine it comes from, such as `goodfetch::rpc::dispatch`:
Experimental (ADR 0132).

LogLevel.description:
The level of the engine's log events a Connection receives: those at
it and above; `off`, the default, receives none.

oneOf.description: State changes, warnings and errors: what `info` logs.
Also a line per request, fetch or command.

MainContent.description: Whether the extractor found the document's main content.

oneOf.description:
The document has none: the formats read from it are empty, a value
and never the whole page in its place.

Managed.description:
What an Operator policy's `[managed]` table holds, which marks the
policy *managed*: deployed by MDM or Ansible, read-only in the Console
(ADR 0031).

ManagedLimit.description:
An install Limit a managed Operator policy names (ADRs 0031 and 0041):
each engine of the policy's major writes it to the Usage ledger when it
starts, as a row of its own keyed by that major and set by
[`LimitSetter::ManagedPolicy`], which only the policy and
`upgrade-files` change.

amount.description:
How much it allows per period: a count of the Usage kind, or
millionths of the currency.

currency.description: The currency it caps the price in, an ISO 4217 code.

period.description: The period it counts over; none for a Limit that never starts again.

MarkdownContent.description: How much of the page a Markdown format holds.

oneOf.description: The main content the extractor finds, the default.

MarkdownFormat.description: The `markdown` format of a request: `true`, or its options.

content.description: How much of the page it holds.

MemoryReading.description: The engine's memory, as the governor read it.

host.description:
The host's own memory pressure: PSI and `MemAvailable` on Linux,
the memory-pressure level on macOS, the low-memory notification on
Windows.

used.description:
What the engine and its children use, in bytes: PSS on Linux, so
pages its browsers share count once.

anyOf.description: A message that expects no reply.

Message.description: Any message of the protocol, as one line of a transcript holds it.

calls.description: The calls, retries and Repairs included.

Navigated.description:
What a navigation answers: the document's response, or none for a
navigation within the same document, to a URL no server answers, such as
`about:blank`, to a file the browser downloads instead of showing, which
`page.download` reports, or back or forward from the last entry of the
page's history. A 404 or a 500 is a response, a value.

NewPageParams.description: What `run.new_page` takes: the Run whose default Session opens the page.

What `run.new_session` takes: the Run whose Session it opens, the
Session's own source and its own settings.

The Session's own settings, nested by key: `filter_lists.ads`,
`.trackers`, `.annoyances`, `.first_party_scripts`,
`browser.block_resources` and `live_view.hiding` choose its pages'
Clean-up rules over the Run's. `session.source` is refused here with `setting_not_applicable`,
as the call's own `source` sets it, and so is any other key, which
only the Run sets.

source.description:
`session.source` for this Session alone: left out, the Run's or the
connection's applies; `null`, the Session opens fresh (ADRs 0083
and 0092).

NotAddedReason.description: Why the Frontier did not add a request (ADRs 0093 and 0120).

The Frontier already admitted a request of the same identity: its

Its URL is outside the crawl's scope (`crawl.scope.*`).
The Run's domain policy refuses its host.

Its URL's scheme is one the crawl cannot fetch: only `http` and
`https` are.

The WHATWG URL Standard's parser refuses its URL, or it is relative

Its URL's path has more segments than `crawl.max_path_segments`.

A segment of its URL's path repeats more than

The engine cannot write the cache, such as a read-only
`GOODFETCH_BROWSERS_PATH` (ADR 0098).

A Limit flagged *must understand* that a Run's engine cannot evaluate,
as the Run stopped for it names it (ADR 0041): its scope, Usage kind,
currency and period as the ledger holds them.

currency.description: The currency it caps a price in, for a price Limit.

period.description: Its period; none for a Limit that never starts again.

NothingCommitted.description: Why a succeeded request committed no Record (ADR 0103).

Every Record it pushed was dropped or rejected, as its `records`
count.

NothingDone.description: Why a call that ends a Run did nothing (ADR 0102's G1).

oneOf.description: The start found the Run ended.

when fetched.
A resume or a retry found nothing left.

Now.description: The word `now`: from the next commit on.

OracleAnswer.description:
An oracle's answer for one Proving ground task: the task, the outcome,
and the rest of the Proving ground's answer as it came (what is missing,
extra or wrong, the tool's status, the oracle's time).

OracleOutcome.description:
The outcome the Proving ground's oracle gives a submitted result, whatever
status the tool reported (ADR 0025).

oneOf.description: Correct but missing Records, without claiming success.
Claimed success with wrong or missing data.
Neither correct nor a claimed success.

The site refused it, with a Block cause.

OutcomeRequest.description: The crawl request an outcome ends.

depth.description: How many links away from a seed it is: 0 for a seed.

anyOf.description: After the outcome at this position, which a reader last read.

turned into a download.

page_id.description: The page whose navigation it was.

suggested_filename.description: The file name the browser suggests for it.

PageEventName.description:
A page's event a program listens to, by its words (ADR 0099): each
SDK joins them as Playwright spells the event, such as `pageerror`.

PageExchange.description:
What `page.response` reports, and `page.wait_for_request_finished`
answers: a request and the response it got.

What `page.load`, `page.dom_content_loaded`, `page.crash` and
`page.close` report: the page whose main frame's document fired the
event, or that crashed or closed.

PageFormats.description:
What `page.formats` answers: the formats the request asked for, and
none it did not, with the document's URL, its base URL and whether it
has main content. Text is as the document holds it, never repaired.

base_url.description:
The URL its relative URLs resolve against: its first `<base href>`,
else its URL.

markdown.description: Its content as Markdown, when the request asked for it.

PageId.description: A page of a Run, named by the engine when it opens it.

PageOnEnded.description: What `page.on` answers when its page goes, closed or with its Run.

PageOnParams.description: What `page.on` takes: the page and the event listened to.

What `run.new_page` and `session.new_page` answer: the page, and the
Session it belongs to, which `page.session()` returns.

session_id.description: Its Session: the Run's default Session for `run.new_page`.

A request of a page, ADR 0085's `Request`: one per hop of a redirect
chain, each hop under the same `request_id`.

headers.description: Its headers as the browser sent them.

is_navigation_request.description: Whether it loads the document of the page's main frame.

The URLs of the hops a redirect led from before it, the first first;
empty when no redirect led to it.

The browser's name for what it loads, such as `Document` or
`Fetch`.

For a navigation's document, the encoding the browser decoded it

headers.description: Its headers, their names lower-cased, as the browser received them.

PageRouteParams.description:
What `page.route` takes: the page, and the URLs whose requests its

What `page.web_socket` reports: a WebSocket the page opened, whose

max_depth.description: How deep a crawl goes, its seeds at depth 0 and each enqueue one level deeper than the request whose attempt added it: a deeper request is not added, with `max_depth`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.

max_path_segments.description: The most segments a URL's path may have, as the WHATWG parser splits it, an empty last segment (a trailing slash) not counted (Heritrix's `maxPathDepth`): a URL with more is not added, with `max_path_segments`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 20 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

max_requests.description: How many requests a crawl admits, its seeds included: once it admitted this many, a further one is not added, with `max_requests`, and a Run that refused one ends `incomplete`. None by default; `null` clears it.

max_segment_repeats.description: How many times back to back a segment of a URL's path, or a run of segments, may appear (Heritrix's `maxRepetitions`), so `/a/a` passes and `/a/a/a` and `/a/b/a/b/a/b` do not, while numbers that recur apart, as in `/page/1/tag/1/sort/1`, do: a URL past it is not added, with `max_segment_repeats`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

max_url_length.description: The longest URL a crawl admits, in characters as the WHATWG parser serializes it, without its fragment (Scrapy's `URLLENGTH_LIMIT`): a longer one is not added, with `max_url_length`, and a finished Run that refused one is `unverified`. 2,083 by default; `null` turns the cap off.

max.description: How many times a work item whose attempt failed retryably is tried again: 2, Scrapy's `RETRY_TIMES`. A run already going takes a tightened Operator policy cap before its next retry.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

drain_grace.description: How long `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, drains on `SIGTERM` before it exits: 110 seconds, below the 120-second `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the Helm chart, which must exceed it. Each run that reaches its next safe point in that time stops with a Checkpoint, resumable by its Run ID; one that does not stays resumable from its run file. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_DAEMON_DRAIN_GRACE` in milliseconds.

idle_timeout.description: How long a Daemon with no connected Client, a visible Console tab included, waits before it stops: 10 minutes. `daemon start --keep-alive`, a held Schedule and an installed service keep it running. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

contexts_per_process.description: How many of a Run's Sessions share one browser process, each in a browser context of its own: 8. The Run's next Session past it gets a process of its own; Sessions of different Runs never share one.

memory_cap.description: The memory, in bytes, of a browser and its processes past which it is recycled; unset by default, when the cap is twice what the browser used once it had opened its first page.

recycle_idle.description: How long a browser may hold no open page before it closes, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage for the browser that replaces it: 5 minutes.

recycle_pages.description: How many pages a browser opens before it is recycled: 100. Recycled, it opens no new page, closes once its pages are done and is replaced, each of its Sessions keeping its cookies and storage.

ceiling.description: The most browser pages the engine's Resource governor admits open at once, across its Runs: 32.

floor.description: The fewest browser pages the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.browser_page.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

critical.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine's memory is critical: 95.

ceiling.description: The most HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 200.

floor.description: The fewest HTTP and discovered-API fetches the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.http.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

last_resort_after.description: How long the engine's memory may stay critical with its concurrency at the floor before the Resource governor reaches its last resort, when a Daemon's `/readyz` fails: 60 s.

memory_allowance.description: The most memory, in bytes, the engine and its children may use, as its Memory allowance when it is tighter than the process's own cgroup limit, its Windows Job object's limit or half of physical memory; unset by default. Read again at every sample.

ceiling.description: The most model calls the engine's Resource governor admits at once, across its Runs: 16.

floor.description: The fewest model calls the engine's Resource governor keeps admitting at once, however loaded the machine: 1. Equal to `governor.model_call.ceiling`, it fixes the concurrency there.

pressure.description: The share of the Memory allowance in use, in percent, from which the engine is under pressure and its Resource governor lowers its concurrency; also the CPU and Tokio workers' busy share from which they hold it: 85.

run_share.description: The share, in percent, of each kind's concurrency one Run may hold at once, at least one: 100. An Operator policy cap bounds every Run's share.

sample_interval.description: How often the engine's Resource governor reads memory, CPU and Tokio saturation, sizes its concurrency and sends `engine.system_info`: every second.

max_files.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_size.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

initial.description: The shortest wait of a domain's backoff: each wait is drawn at random between it and three times the previous wait (the first between it and three times it), never above `politeness.backoff.max`: 2 s. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.

max.description: The longest wait of a domain's backoff: 60 s. A `Retry-After` may hold the domain longer, up to `politeness.retry_after.max`. A shorter value is listed in the run's result.

concurrency.description: How many requests may be in flight at once on one domain key, counted across every run of the user that shares Politeness: a run admits one only while that combined count is below its own value. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1.

delay.description: How long a run waits after the last request start on a domain key, by any run of the user that shares Politeness, before it starts another there. None by default until the fetch tiers set ADR 0086's default of 1 s.

max.description: The longest a crawl waits for the time a site's `Retry-After` asks, past `politeness.backoff.max`: 15 minutes. When the site asks for longer, nothing is sent to its domain before that time and nothing waits for it: the request whose response asked, and each request admitted to the domain meanwhile, ends `failed` with `response_unavailable`, and `run.retry_failed` re-admits them once the site is back. Whatever its value, nothing is sent sooner than the site asked.

attempt_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports let a connection attempt to one of a host's addresses run before they start the next one beside it: 250 ms, RFC 8305's Connection Attempt Delay. An attempt that fails starts the next at once.

resolution_delay.description: How long the engine's HTTP transports wait for a host's IPv6 addresses once its IPv4 addresses arrived first, before they start connecting over IPv4: 50 ms, RFC 8305's Resolution Delay.

echo_repeats.description: How many times the sample operation repeats a text.

max_age.description: How long after it opened a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3,000 s, Crawlee's `maxAgeSecs`.

max_error_score.description: The error score at which a Session of a crawl's Session pool is retired: 3. A block or a failed Page check adds 1, a success takes 0.5 off, never below 0 (Crawlee's model).

max_size.description: How many Sessions a crawl's Session pool keeps open at once: 100. A request goes to a new Session while the pool has room, then to one drawn among those open.

max_uses.description: How many requests one Session of a crawl's Session pool serves before it is retired: 50, Crawlee's `maxUsageCount`.

critical_free.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `critical` storage level: every Run with an essential write on it stops resumably at its next safe point, with `resource: "storage"`, and a new Run whose run file would go there is refused with `resources_exhausted`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 1 GiB and 2 % of its size, and free inodes go by 2 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

low_free.description: The free space, in bytes, below which a filesystem a Run writes to is at the `low` storage level: its Runs go on, record no Run trace video, store no new Response cache entry, skip their periodic Checkpoints onto it, and carry the warning `storage_low`. Unset, each filesystem takes the smaller of 5 GiB and 10 % of its size, and free inodes go by 10 %; `0` turns the level off, which the Run's report lists in `weakened`. Read again at every sample of the Resource governor; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

action.description: How long a locator action waits for its target to be unique and actionable, and replays a gesture that landed elsewhere, before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, or `target_not_unique` for a target still ambiguous: 30 s.

close.description: How long a stop of a Run, `run.stop` or a scope's close, waits for its next safe point before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`, the Run still stopping there: 30 s.

first_byte.description: How long a request may wait for its response's first byte before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

handler.description: How long a crawl's handler has for one attempt, which also bounds every action inside it, and from which a work item's lease is derived: the timeout plus the larger of 10 s and a tenth of it. 60 s, Crawlee's `requestHandlerTimeoutSecs`.

navigation.description: How long a navigation may take before its attempt fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s, Playwright's default.

run.description: How long a Run may go on before it checkpoints and stops at its next safe point, resumable; none by default.

secret.description: How long a Secret provider may take to answer one reference before the resolution fails with `secret_unavailable`, `failure: "timed_out"`: 30 s.

wait.description: How long a wait for an application state, such as `page.wait_for_request_finished`, may take before it fails with `deadline_exceeded`: 30 s.

lock.description: The values it sets and locks: no higher layer changes them.

max_requests_per_minute.description: How many requests a Run admits in a minute at most, spaced evenly (GCRA), whatever its concurrency; none by default. An Operator policy cap bounds it even when unset, and a run already going takes a tightened cap at its next admission.

block_resources.description: The resource kinds the Session's pages never load, failed as `BlockedByClient` by its interception before every navigation: any of `image`, `media`, `font` and `stylesheet`; none by default. The never-block list still loads a challenge's own. In `standard` and `stealth` the Run warns once per Session that the site can see the missing loads.

headless.description: Whether the Session's Chromium runs with no window: `true` by default. Headless or not, the site sees one browser's identity, with no `HeadlessChrome` token in its user agent.

max_unused_age.description: How long a Pinned artifact no installed executable pins stays in the Browser cache unused before the clean-up deletes it, and how long an executable's entry counts as installed after it was last seen: 30 days. `null` turns the automatic clean-up off. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

interval.description: How often a live Run writes a Checkpoint where the engine keeps its Checkpoints, on the engine's clock; none by default locally.

domains.description: The domains whose consent prompts a run accepts instead of refusing. A Recipe or a run only narrows it; it is widened only in configuration or by a person's answer.

handling.description: Whether a browser Session answers Consent prompts: on by default in every Access mode, refusing each prompt in every frame and hiding one with no refusal that leaves the content readable. Off stops only the answering.

address.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console, as `host:port`: `127.0.0.1` on port 7800 plus the major (7700 plus the minor during `0.y` previews), so each major's Console has its own port. Port 0 takes a free port, which the Daemon's runtime file and `daemon status` report. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

content_address.description: Where the Daemon serves the Console's content origin, which shows scraped HTML, screenshots, DOM snapshots and page bodies, as `host:port`. None by default: the Console's host on a free port, or, when `console.content_public_url` is set, the Console's own listener, which tells the two origins apart by the `Host` each request names. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

content_public_url.description: The origin a browser reaches the Console's content origin at behind a proxy, such as `https://content.example.com`, which the addresses the Console signs name. None by default: the content origin's own listener. With no `console.content_address`, the content origin shares the Console's listener and answers the requests that name this origin's host. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

idle_expiry.description: How long a Console sign-in lasts without being used, in milliseconds: 30 days. Each use starts it again; a sign-in unused for longer ends, and its person signs in again. Set in an Operator policy only.

rate.description: How many times one address may try to sign in to the Console in a minute: 10. A further attempt in that minute is refused, whatever its credential. Set in an Operator policy only.

domain_keys.description: Host names, each with the domain key its requests and those of the hosts under it share, the longest name winning, in place of the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List: a Recipe's override of the key its per-domain queues use. None by default.

handler_failed.description: Whether a work item whose handler failed with `handler_failed` is tried again: `false`.

sample_pages.description: How many pages the sample crawl visits.

exclude.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, none of which a link may match, besides `crawl.scope.strategy` and `crawl.scope.include`. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.

include.description: URL patterns, each a glob read as Playwright reads one and matched in the engine, of which a link must match one when there are any, besides `crawl.scope.strategy`, which they never replace. None by default. Fixed for a Run's life.

strategy.description: What a crawl's links are measured by against every seed, on every enqueue, redirect and Hook rewrite: `same_hostname` (Crawlee's default), `same_domain` (the registrable domain under the Public Suffix List), `same_origin` or `all`. report_guarantee_class.description: Every delivery reports its Guarantee class, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

write_ids_and_epochs.description: Every write a Sink makes carries its delivery ID and run epoch, an honesty guarantee that stays locked whatever the layer.

allowed_domains.description: The hosts a run's requests may reach: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched on the host as a browser's URL parser leaves it (punycode, dotted-decimal IPv4), and `*` every host, only when written. `["*"]` by default; set for a connection or a Run. A request to a host it does not list fails with `egress_refused`.

blocked_domains.description: The hosts no request of a run may reach, whatever `egress.allowed_domains` allows: each entry its host and their subdomains, matched as `egress.allowed_domains` matches, and `*` every host. Empty by default; set for a connection or a Run. A request to a host it lists fails with `egress_refused`.

offline.description: Whether the engine opens no connection nobody configured: every pinned download, such as a Pinned artifact missing from the Browser cache, fails with `artifact_unavailable_offline` before it connects, naming the command that supplies it beforehand. `false` by default; set at every layer, and an Operator policy can lock it.

ads.description: Whether a browser Session blocks ads by EasyList, as a blocker does: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.

annoyances.description: Whether a browser Session blocks page annoyances (social widgets, newsletter and notification prompts) by Fanboy Annoyance, its cookie sections left to the Consent prompt runner: on by default in every Access mode.

extra.description: Extra Filter lists, by URL or path. Their scriptlets run only when the value comes from an Operator policy or user or project configuration; from a Recipe or a run, only their blocking rules apply.

first_party_scripts.description: Whether a site's own scripts load whatever the Filter lists say: off by default.

page_scriptlets.description: Whether the Filter lists' scriptlets that patch a page's JavaScript run, from uBlock Origin's resources downloaded with the lists that name them: off by default, since a site can see them.

trackers.description: Whether a browser Session blocks trackers by EasyPrivacy: on by default in every Access mode. A blocked request fails as `BlockedByClient`; the never-block list keeps challenge, anti-bot, anti-fraud and payment scripts loading.

hiding.description: Whether a Session's pages hide, on the live page, the elements the Filter lists' cosmetic rules match: `auto` (the default) and `always` hide them through a style sheet the site cannot see on Chromium, in every frame and every new document; `off` leaves the live page as served. When the guard finds an action's target hidden, it lifts the rule for the Session and acts. Extracted content has the elements removed whatever this says.

max_files.description: How many log files an engine process keeps where `log.output` is `file`, the one it writes included: 5, so a Daemon's logs stay under about 50 MiB. The oldest goes at each rotation. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

max_size.description: The size, in bytes, at which an engine process's log file rotates where `log.output` is `file`: 10 MiB. A file holds at most this much and one line more. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

format.description: How an engine process writes its logs on stderr, or on stdout under `daemon run`: `text`, lines for a person reading a terminal, or `json`, JSON lines. Unset, the logs are text on stderr and JSON lines on stdout under `daemon run`; a log file holds JSON lines whatever it says. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

level.description: Which of its logs an engine process writes: `info`, the default, which logs state changes only (a Run started, resumed or stopped, a domain backing off, a storage level changing, a Daemon draining) and never one line per request, or any `tracing` filter directive, such as `warn` or `info,goodfetch::rpc=debug`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

output.description: Where an engine process writes its logs beside stderr: `stdout`, JSON lines for the platform to collect and rotate, `file`, JSON lines in its own files of the Goodfetch home's log folder, rotated at `log.file.max_size` and kept to `log.file.max_files`, or `none`. Unset, it is `stdout` under `daemon run`, `file` for every other Daemon and `none` for an Attached engine, whose logs go to its Client as log events; `stdout` on an Attached engine, whose stdout is its protocol, fails with `setting_not_applicable`. Read when the process starts; set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

resolve.description: Host names mapped to addresses before any lookup, in the engine's resolver and in Chromium, each address still checked by ADR 0017's resolved-address rule. Empty by default; an Operator policy can lock it.

Unset by default: no ops listener and no Prometheus export. Any address, so a cluster's probes and scrapers reach it; a request whose `Host` is a name other than `localhost`, or that carries an `Origin`, is refused. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy, or for `daemon run` through `GOODFETCH_OPS_ADDRESS`.

metrics_endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint `daemon run`, the foreground Daemon, exports its metrics to, in protobuf, every 60 seconds and once more as it exits: a full URL such as `http://collector:4318/v1/metrics`. Unset by default: nothing is exported (ADR 0043).

traces_endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP endpoint an engine process exports its `tracing` spans to, such as `http://localhost:4318/v1/traces`; unset, the default, exports nothing, and nothing leaves the machine. The spans cover each run, page and CDP command, with glossary IDs and bounded values as fields and a URL as its origin. Span names, span fields and the engine's targets are Experimental: a minor may change them, and its release notes list the change. Set in user configuration or an Operator policy only.

chain_rpc_endpoints.description: The RPC endpoint of each chain whose finalized state proves a payment did not settle, by chain. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

domains.description: The registrable domains a run may pay for a page; `*` only when written. Widened only in an Operator policy, user or project configuration, or by a person's answer; a Recipe or a run only narrows it.

exchange_rates.description: The fixed rates that convert a price into a Limit's currency, by currency pair. Set only in an Operator policy and user and project configuration.

max_price_per_page.description: The most a run pays for one page, as an amount and its currency such as `0.05 USD`; none by default. Raised only in configuration; a Recipe or a run only lowers it.

enabled.description: Whether a domain that answers 429, 502, 503 or 504, or does not answer in time, is backed off, and its `Retry-After` waited out, for every run of the user that shares Politeness. Off, the run ignores both, and it is listed in the run's result.
